prompts.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: main method figure for an anonymous CVPR research paper, a very wide landscape diagram, approximately 2.6:1 aspect ratio, crisp high-resolution white background.
Primary request: Draw a beautiful, technically precise publication-quality method overview of a music-to-TEXT choreography system. Exact heading: "HereWeChoreography". Use a restrained scientific visual language, muted teal, amber, lavender and navy, thin tidy arrows, generous white space, consistent large readable English labels. Not a slide, no decorative gradients or logos.
Composition: A left-to-right main path with FIVE explicitly numbered panels in order, in one row; a smaller shared-context lane across the top and a small feedback loop across the bottom.
Panel 1 heading "1  Music evidence". Show a clean waveform and beat/downbeat ticks below it, labeled "Music + downbeats".
Panel 2 heading "2  Bar-aligned units". Show four adjacent colored windows of unequal widths, each containing 2–4 bars, with the exact small label "2–4 bars per unit". This is musical bar grouping, not learned phrase recognition.
Panel 3 heading "3  Local primitives". Show a compact stack of 2 candidate text cards, each with a simple human movement silhouette, labeled "Shared candidate cache". Add one short example "Step left; sweep the right arm". These are TEXT descriptions, not retrieved 3D motions.
Panel 4 heading "4  Compositional harness". This is the widest central panel. Include three tidy stacked modules labeled "Segment objectives", "Motif memory" and "Contextual composition". Inside the motif module use small tokens A, A′, B, A″. Show an input arrow from shared context and an arrow from accepted history into composition. A small badge inside says "Bounded calls".
Panel 5 heading "5  Choreography score". Show a vertical time axis and three compact text events on a paper-like card, with tiny timestamps and movement lines. Use readable short labels "Timed action text" and "Dance style is hip-hop." at the top of this output card. Do not show skeleton generation, video output, or a finished rendered dancer.
Top shared-context lane: from music evidence to a slim context box labeled "Global style + acoustic summaries", then a down arrow into panel 4. Make clear the external local model analyzes actual audio while the composer uses shared summaries and candidates.
Bottom feedback lane: a slim panel labeled "Validate → target repetitive spans → revise". Arrow from panel 4 down into this panel then looping back to panel 4. Next to it a lock icon with label "Retain accepted context". This depicts targeted TEXT revision, not learned physical motion synthesis.
Constraints: All panels must follow numerical left-to-right order. Keep font sizes large enough for a full-width two-column paper figure. No dataset names, counts, implementation paths, unsupported learned compatibility model, 3D transition synthesis, performance plots, paper author names, or numerical experimental claims. Do not duplicate panel headings. Keep English wording exactly as requested. Non-numeric waveforms and diagrams are illustrative.

Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: a publication-quality wide scientific explanatory diagram for a CVPR paper, landscape approximately 2.7:1, white background. Match a restrained muted teal/amber/lavender/navy palette, thin precise lines, clean large sans-serif typography, elegant flat silhouettes and action cards.
Primary request: Illustrate the representation and targeted revision of TEXTUAL choreography, not a motion rendering pipeline. No fabricated experimental results. Heading "Composing and revising movement primitives".
Layout: Two rows with a clear left-to-right order and aligned musical windows, plus a small state card on the left.
Left narrow card heading "Composition context", with three readable entries "Segment objective", "Accepted history", "Style condition". Add a lock icon beside accepted history.
Upper main row heading "Initial text score". Draw four consecutive pale time-window cards, all same conceptual sequence. Card labels "A", "A", "B", "A". Under the first A use short action text "Step left + right-arm sweep"; second A same text; B "Lower + turn"; final A same step/sweep phrase. These are illustrative synthetic text examples. Put compact generic movement silhouettes inside cards as visual explanations. Do not print timestamps or numeric measurements. A dashed amber outline encloses the second A with label "Potential redundant copy". Another small note below first/last A says "Motif return may be intentional".
Middle slender strip shows an arrow down from the highlighted A to a small revision operation box with exact labels "Change only the selected span" and "Check time bounds and constraints". Include a two-headed small relation arrow between neighboring cards with label "Written boundary context". Show locks on the three unchanged cards and only unlock the selected second card. Do not imply the exact repetition detector universally distinguishes artistic quality; make "potential" visible.
Lower main row heading "Targeted text revision". Four aligned cards now labeled "A", "A′", "B", "A". First A and final A retain exact step/sweep text. A′ text "Step right + low arm sweep"; B unchanged. Highlight only A′ in teal and show one concise note beneath, "Direction / level / coordination". At bottom show short caption "Protected regions stay fixed; revision consumes the remaining call budget."
Constraints: Minimal yet detailed enough to understand the method; readable at paper width; no axes with fabricated values, no performance improvements, no action-quality scores, no 3D physics claims, no audio-to-motion generation. All output is choreography TEXT, with silhouettes only illustrative. Keep first, third and fourth cards visually identical before/after. Do not add dataset construction, internal filenames, data counts, model names, or author information.
